title: Sharing your work
summary: Push a branch to origin, then pull a teammate's commit.

say.never: Your project folder is the **local** copy. Teams also keep a shared copy on a server, like **GitHub**, called the **remote**. The remote is usually named **origin**. You work locally, then **push** to send your commits up, and **pull** to bring teammates' commits down. In this lesson `origin` is a private copy on this computer, so no account is needed.
say.bit: Local = your copy. Remote (`origin`) = the shared copy on GitHub. Push uploads, pull downloads. Here `origin` is a hidden local copy.

say.never: Open **Source Control** (the branch icon on the left). Each exercise folder has its own section there. Click **06-push** so the buttons and menus work on that folder.
say.bit: In Source Control, click **06-push** so the buttons act on it.

say.never: Check the branch name in the bottom-left says `issue-18-team-colors`. Open the **...** menu in Source Control, choose **Pull, Push**, then **Push to...**, and pick `origin`.
say.bit: On `issue-18-team-colors`: **...** menu, Pull, Push, Push to..., `origin`.

say.never: Now click **07-pull** in Source Control and check the branch is `develop`. Open the **...** menu, choose **Pull, Push**, then **Pull**. Open `Schedule.txt`: your teammate's line is there.
say.bit: Click **07-pull** (on `develop`): **...** menu, Pull, Push, **Pull**. `Schedule.txt` gets your teammate's line.

say.never: Open the lesson chip and press **Verify** for **Push** and **Pull**.
